source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 1066 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 1066 was established by Ordinance No. 31991, passed by the Dallas City Council on August 11, 2021. (Ord. 31991)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 1066 is established on property located at the southwest corner of Midway Road and Killion Drive. The size of PD 1066 is approximately 6.935 acres. (Ord. 31991)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 31991)

sections.title: Exhibits
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 1066A: development plan.

(2) Exhibit 1066B: traffic management plan.

(3) Exhibit 1066C: landscape plan. (Ord. 31991)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 1066A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) For all other uses, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51A-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. 31991)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the R-16(A) Single Family District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the R-16(A) Single Family District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the R- 16(A) Single Family District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the R-16(A) Single Family District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) The following additional main use is permitted by right:

-- Public school other than an open-enrollment charter school. (Ord. 31991)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.107. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. 31991)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the R-16(A) Single Family District apply.

(b) Public school other than an open-enrollment charter school.

(1) Front yard. Parking is allowed in the required front yard.

(2) Height.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, maximum structure height is 35 feet. Mechanical equipment may project an additional 10 feet above the maximum structure height.

(B) For the area on the development plan labelled “New 3-story Addition” maximum structure height is 48 feet. An elevator penthouse or stair bulkhead may project an additional two feet above the maximum structure height.

(C) Building heights are shown on the development plan.

(D) If any portion of a structure is over 26 feet in height, that portion may not be located above a residential proximity slope. Except for chimneys, structures listed in Section 51A-4.408(a)(2) may project through the slope to a height not to exceed the maximum structure height, or 12 feet above the slope, whichever is less. Chimneys may project through the slope to a height 12 feet above the slope and 12 feet above the maximum structure height.

(3) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 48 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not. (Ord. 31991)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Public school other than an open-enrollment charter school.

(1) Required parking. A maximum of 110 parking spaces must be provided for a high school containing up to 50 classrooms. Parking must be provided in accordance with Division 51A-4.200 for any classrooms in excess of 50.

(2) Student parking prohibited. Students must arrive and depart campus on transportation provided by the public school district or an authorized representative. Students are not allowed to park on campus.

(3) Remote parking for school related events. It is anticipated that throughout the school year there will be occasional school related events that will be held on the campus not during school hours. Examples include, but are not limited to, “Meet the Teacher” events, award ceremonies, or new student/parent orientation. These type of events are limited to non-regular school hours and must end at 10:00 p.m. With the limited amount of on campus parking, DISD shall provide shuttle service for these events. The type of vehicle used for the shuttle service will vary depending on the type of event. Remote parking for the event may be provided either at the home school for the student or at the Thomas Jefferson High School/Walnut Hill International Leadership Academy campus. Shuttle service must be provided approximately 30 minutes before, during, and 30 minutes after the event. Information provided to students, parents, and other possible participants in any school related event must specify that no parking is allowed on campus and remote parking will be provided with a shuttle service. Parking areas on campus for school related events are limited to school personnel. (Ord. Nos. 31991; 32155)

sections.title: Traffic Management Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.110. TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN.

(a) In general. Operation of a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school must comply with the traffic management plan (Exhibit 1066B).

(b) Traffic study.

(1) The Property owner or operator shall prepare a traffic study evaluating the sufficiency of the traffic management plan. The initial traffic study must be submitted to the director by May 21, 2025. After the initial traffic study, the Property owner or operator shall submit updates of the traffic study to the director by March 1 of each odd-numbered year.

(2) The traffic study must be in writing, performed by a licensed engineer, based on a minimum of four samples taken on different school days at different drop-off and pick- up times over a two-week period, and must contain an analysis of the following:

(A) ingress and egress points;

(B) queue lengths;

(C) number and location of personnel assisting with loading and unloading of students;

(D) drop-off and pick-up locations;

(E) drop-off and pick-up hours for each grade level;

(F) hours for each grade level; and

(G) circulation.

(3) Within 30 days after submission of a traffic study, the director shall determine if the current traffic management plan is sufficient.

(A) If the director determines that the current traffic management plan is sufficient, the director shall notify the applicant in writing.

(B) If the director determines that the current traffic management plan results in traffic hazards or traffic congestion, the director shall require the Property owner to submit an amended traffic management plan. If the Property owner fails to submit an amended traffic management plan within 30 days, the director shall notify the city plan commission.

(c) Amendment process.

(1) A traffic management plan may be amended using the minor plan amendment fee and public hearing process in Section 51A-1.105(k)(3).

(2) The city plan commission shall authorize changes in a traffic management plan if the proposed amendments improve queuing or traffic circulation; eliminate traffic hazards; or decrease traffic congestion. (Ord. 31991)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, see Article VI.

(b) Noise.

(1) The noise level from the chillers at the surrounding bounding lot line must not exceed the limits allowed for a residential zoning district.

(2) A sound dampening wall and landscape screening must be installed around the chillers to reduce noise levels as shown on the development plan and landscape plan.

(3) Noise dampening features provided by the manufacturer of the chiller units must be implemented and installed.

(c) Lighting. Except in emergency situations, use of temporary generator light towers are prohibited. (Ord. 31991)

sections.title: Landscaping And Urban Forest Conservation
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.112. LANDSCAPING AND URBAN FOREST CONSERVATION.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Public school other than an open-enrollment charter school.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit 1066C). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the landscape plan, the text of this article controls.

(2) All new required trees located within 30 feet of Killion Drive or Fieldfare Drive, as shown on the landscape plan, must be evergreen, as approved by the building official.

(3) A replacement tree must have a caliper of at least three inches.

(4) After the Property is in compliance with the landscape plan, the Property owner or operator shall provide an annual health assessment prepared by a licensed arborist of all trees and landscaping on the Property to the city arborist.

(c) Maintenance. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 31991)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.113. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 31991)

sections.title: Outdoor Lighting
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.114. OUTDOOR LIGHTING.

(a) Maximum heights for outdoor lighting are as follows:

(1) Parking lot lighting. 25 feet.

(2) Parking lot lighting within 100 feet of residential zoning. 15 feet.

(3) Security lighting. 25 feet.

(4) Security lighting within 100 feet of residential zoning. 15 feet.

(5) Pedestrian lighting. 10 feet.

(6) Pole mounted security lighting. 12 feet.

(7) Building mounted lighting. 15 feet.

(b) All outdoor lighting must be directed downward and away from adjacent properties.

(c) Lighting may not produce glare or direct illumination across a property line of an intensity that creates a nuisance or detracts from the use or enjoyment of adjacent property.

(d) Building mounted security light fixtures such as wall packs may not project above the roof line of the building and must be shielded. (Ord. 31991)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.115. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) In general. The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Compliance. Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Bus idling. Buses are not allowed to idle their engines without passengers for more than 15 minutes while on the Property or the adjacent right-of-way.

(d) Protection. The original facade of the Spanish title roof building existing on September 9, 2021 is encouraged to be protected.

(e) Screening. Roof mounted equipment must be screened by a solid screen with a minimum height of the equipment or setback a minimum of 30 feet from the edge of the building.

(f) Notification. Before submitting an application for a minor amendment or zoning change, the school shall notify property owners in the notification area 30 days prior to submitting the application through the President of the Walnut Hill Homeowners Association (WHHA), Walnut Meadows Homeowners Associations, and Walnut Ridge Association (WRA) by electronic communication. Proof of notification must be submitted to the city with the zoning application. (Ord. 31991)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1066.116. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31991)
